stem: Which of the following is a non-contact force ?
expl: Non-contact forces act on objects without the need for physical contact. For example : Gravitational force – The force of attraction between any two objects with mass, causing objects to fall towards the Earth. Magnetic force – The force exerted by magnets, causing them to attract or repel to each other. Electric force – The force exerted by electric charges, causing them to attract or repel each other. On the other hand, contact forces require physical contact between objects for the force to act. Frictional force and impact or applied force are examples of contact force.

stem: The energy of wind is –
expl: All moving things have kinetic energy. It is energy possessed by an object due to its motion or movement. Wind energy is the kinetic energy of air in motion. The kinetic energy of the wind (wind energy) can be converted into mechanical and electrical energy.

stem: In wind power, which form of energy is converted into electrical energy?
expl: The term wind energy or wind power describes the process by which the wind is used to generate mechanical power or electricity. Wind turbines convert the kinetic energy of the wind into mechanical power. This mechanical power can be used for specific tasks such as grinding grain or pumping water or a generator can convert this mechanical power into electricity.

stem: Which of the following energy changes involves frictional force?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Frictional forces apply in a static condition as well as in a moving condition. The respective co-efficient of friction are called static co-efficient and dynamic co-efficient. While in the static condition, there is no displacement i.e. no work done and hence no energy conversion. It is in the dynamic condition, there is movement against the frictional force that there is energy loss by way of heat. In other words, kinetic energy of movement is converted into heat. Energy conversion due to friction does not involve change in potential energy/chemical energy. Even when an object is falling in air, its potential energy first gets converted into kinetic energy and then heat or sound etc. In battery, its chemical energy is converted into electrical energy as well as heat but friction has nothing to do in such conversion.

stem: Who is the first person to define speed?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Italian physicist Galileo Galilei is usually credited with being the first to measure speed by considering the distance covered and the time it takes. Galileo defined speed as the distance covered per unit of time. In equation form, that is v = d/t (where v is speed, d is distance, and t is time). After that Newton propounded the laws of motion to describe the motion of bodies and objects.

stem: Newton's first law of motion is known as :
expl: Newton's first law of motion is also known as 'Law of Inertia' It states that, if an object is at rest or moving at a constant speed in a straight line, it will remain at rest or keep moving in a straight line at constant speed unless acted upon by an unbalanced force. Inertia is the tendency of an object to remain in a state of rest or uniform motion unless a force acts upon it.

stem: As the train starts moving, the head of the passenger sitting inside leans backward because of –
expl: According to the Newton's first law of motion sometimes referred to as the law of inertia which states that an object at rest stays at rest and in motion remain in motion with same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an external force. When a train suddenly starts, the passenger tends to fall backward. This is because the lower part of the body which is in contact with the train begins to move while the upper part of the body tends to maintain its position due to inertia of rest. As a result, the upper part tends to fall backward.

stem: A bus is moving along a straight path and takes a sharp turn to the right side suddenly. The passengers sitting in the bus will :

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: If a bus is moving along a straight path and takes a sharp turn to the right side suddenly, then the passengers sitting on the bus will bend towards the left side. Initially, the passengers and the bus both are moving in the same direction. When the bus suddenly takes a right turn, the lower portion of passengers who are in contact with the bus tends to move in that direction but the upper portion of the passengers will be thrown towards the left. This is because of inertia of direction.

stem: We apply a force of 200 Newtons on a wooden Box and push it on the floor at constant velocity. The marginal friction force will be:
expl: Constant velocity means the acceleration (rate of change of velocity) of the wooden box is zero. According to Newton’s first and second laws of motion, if the acceleration of an object is zero, then the net (resultant) force on it is also zero. Here, the two main horizontal forces are: 1. Applied force in the forward direction = 200 N. 2. Kinetic frictional force in the backward direction (marginal frictional force; exerted by the floor on the wooden box) Since the resultant force is zero; therefore, kinetic frictional force = 200 N. Hence, in this situation the kinetic frictional force (marginal frictional force) acting backward on the box will be 200 newtons, which is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the applied force.

stem: A goalkeeper in a game of football pulls his hands backwards after holding the ball shot at the goal. This enables the goalkeeper to :

options.label: b
options.text: exert large force on the ball

options.label: c
options.text: increase the force exerted by the ball on hands

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: According to Newton's second law, F = m × a or, F = m (v – u)/t So, by pulling his hands backwards, the goalkeeper increases time to hold the ball. By increasing the time, he decreases the force (rate of change of momentum) applied by the football on him. In other words, the goalkeeper pulls his hands backward while holding the ball shot at the goal to reduce the rate of change of momentum which in turn reduces the force exerted on the hands by the ball.

stem: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. The law was given by :

The statement means that in every interaction, there is a pair of forces acting on the two interacting objects. The size of the force on the first object equals the size of the force on the second object. The direction of the force on the first object is opposite to the direction of the force on the second object.

stem: Centripetal force is responsible to :

options.label: a
options.text: independent motion of the object in space

options.label: b
options.text: keep the body moving along the circular path

options.label: c
options.text: fly the object along a straight line

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Newton's first law of motion states that an object moving at constant speed will continue that motion unless acted on by an outside force. This means that circular motion can only happen if there is a 'centre seeking' force – otherwise things would just travel in a straight line, rather than the curved line of a circule. Centripetal means 'centre seeking', so centripetal force is used to refer to the force experienced by an object travelling in a circle. For example, when someone spins a ball attached to a rope horizontally above his head, the rope transmits a centripetal force from the muscles of the hand and arm, causing the ball to move in a circular path. In the special case of the Earth's circular motion around the Sun – or any satellite's circular motion around any celestial body – the centripetal force causing the motion is the result of the gravitational attraction between them.

stem: An effective Coriolis force results from :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In physics, the Coriolis force is an inertial or fictitious force that acts on objects in motion within a frame of reference that rotates with respect to an inertial frame. In popular (non-technical) usage of the term 'Coriolis effect', the rotating reference frame implied is almost always the Earth. An effective Coriolis force is caused due to rotation of the Earth. This force causes moving objects on the surface of the Earth to be deflected to the right (with respect to the direction of travel) in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere.

options.label: d

expl: The purpose of a ball bearing is to reduce rotational friction and support radial and axial loads. Due to ball bearing, the effective area of contact between the wheel and axle is reduced and hence, the frictional force also reduced.

stem: Ball bearings are used to convert static friction into:

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Ball bearings are types of rolling-elements bearings that carry loads, reduce friction, and position moving machine parts while facilitating motion. The purpose of a ball bearing is to reduce rotational friction and support radial and axial loads. It achieves this by using at least two races to contain the balls and transmit the loads through the balls. In most applications, one race is stationary and the other is attached to the rotating assembly (e.g., a hub or shaft). As one of the bearing races rotates it causes the balls to rotate as well. Because the balls are rolling they have a much lower coefficient of friction than if two flat surfaces were sliding against each other. They reduce surface contact and friction across moving planes. Thus, ball bearings are used to convert static friction into rolling friction.

Which of these statements are correct ?
expl: In case of object moving along a circular path two types of forces centripetal and centrifugal acts upon it. As they have opposite impact thus the object remains in balance. If a four wheeler on a circular path is moving faster than the relative speed then it skids outwards but then the frictional force provides the necessary centripetal force which ensures the car to have a curved path. On sharp circular path, if the outer portion of the road is not raised, then the vehicle with high speed will skid outwards and will overturn about its outer wheels.

stem: A truck starts from rest down a hill with a constant acceleration. It achieves 400 meters in 20 seconds, If the weight of the truck is 7 tons then what will be the force acting on it?
expl: For motion with uniform acceleration, the formula is: s = ut + 2 at² where, s – distance covered Here, u = 0, so: s = 2 at² a – acceleration Therefore, 400 = 2 × a × (20)² 400 = 2 × a × 400 400 = 200a Hence, the acceleration of the truck a = 2 m/s². Now, according to Newton’s second law of motion Force: F = ma where, m is mass Mass = 7 tonnes = 7000 kg So, F = ma = 7000 × 2 = 14000 N Thus, the force acting on the truck will be 14000 newtons.

stem: A pair of Oxen exerts a force of 140 newton while ploughing the field. The field ploughed is 15 meter long. The work done in ploughing the length of the fieldis:
expl: In physics, the work done by a constant force is given as follows : W = F × s × cos θ Where, F = applied force (in newtons) s = displacement/distance (in metres) W = work done (in joules) θ = angle between the directions of force and displacement Given that, F = 140 newtons Length of the field (displacement) = 15 metres The oxen pull the plough along the length of the field, so force and displacement are in the same direction. Therefore, cos θ = cos 0° = 1  W = 140 × 15 × 1 = 2100 joules Hence, the work done in pulling the plough through 15 metres is 2100 joules.
